Case 2 (gts-ucdz): bare email assignee -- same output as the @-sigil form.

ACT-304: jane@example.com finish the report (Open)

Case 3 (gts-ucdz): PERSON chip assignee -- identity wins over a login-style guess.

ACT-305: {{chip:jane@example.com}} finish the report (Open)

Case 4 (gts-ucdz, ADR-0027 rule 2): a literal pipe inside action text is not a field delimiter.

ACT-306: jane@example.com approve the design doc, please | thanks (Open)

Case 5 (gts-ucdz): a status token with trailing prose on the same line is preserved as action text.

ACT-307: jane@example.com ship it (Open) - done

Case 6 (gts-ucdz, ADR-0027 rule 4 as refined by gts-v0py): no status token is present -- the parenthesized word in the action text is literal, since what follows it begins with a word character. Authored in its statusless form, so the establishing sync must materialize (Open) at the end of the header line rather than adopt (draft).

[**ACT-308: **](https://northlakeuu.org/NUUTS?cmd=preview&docId=DOC_ID&ain=ACT-308){{chip:jane@example.com}} (draft) proposal (Open)

Case 7 (gts-ucdz, gts-jxrw): a bare token line with nothing else. ADR-0027's actionBody production admits empty text, so this is a VALID action, not a rule-6 unparseable paragraph: it is registered with an empty action text and no assignee, and the establishing sync materializes its status the same way it does for any other statusless record.

[**ACT-309: **](https://northlakeuu.org/NUUTS?cmd=preview&docId=DOC_ID&ain=ACT-309) (Open)

AI-310: jane@example.com legacy spelling still works (Open)
